sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The Baal Shem Tov's interpretation of the verse "Blow the shofar in the month" teaches that one's service must always be with renewal, not as a fixed habit.

translations.translation: And behold, there is a known precise point of our teacher the Baal Shem Tov
(in Kesser Shem Tov6)
regarding this verse,
that it should have said "Blow a shofar in the month."
And the Baal Shem Tov explained this,
that a person should constantly see that he be "in the month" — meaning to renew good deeds, that it should not be like a fixed routine.
And one can explain the matter,
that since this verse speaks about a fundamental and general matter,
the matter of Rosh HaShanah and the matter of "Make Me king over you,"
therefore it contains a fundamental and general instruction in the general service of each and every Jew,
that the service must be in a manner of renewal,
that at every time and every moment and in every single thing he does,
he should do it as something truly new7.
[And perhaps one can add to this further,
that this is also the precise meaning of the word "Tik'u" (blow),
"Tik'u" also from the term strength and might8,
that he should embed himself with the greatest strength and might without any changes in his service,
until he embeds himself in an eternal manner,
so that through this every moment of his service is a new thing].
And with this one can explain the connection to what was said previously in the teaching of the Baal Shem Tov there,
that the matter of a miracle is that the thing was renewed for the first time, and when it comes repeatedly it is called nature — meaning that in truth everything is a miracle.
And one can connect this with the teaching of the Baal Shem Tov9
that every thing in the world is renewed at every moment,
and what is called by the name "nature" is only because the renewal already occurred previously
(and was not renewed now for the first time).

And through contemplation on this very matter — that in truth everything is a miracle and a new thing — this gives power to every matter in service, that he should do it in a manner of something truly new.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The term "Keseh" means a fixed time and season, and on Rosh HaShanah the renewal of time and space is completed through the creation of Adam.

translations.translation: And it continues afterward in the maamar
there,
that the explanation of "Keseh" is
(also)
a term for time and season10,
that there is a limited time and season to draw down the aspect of Malchus.
And one must explain the connection of this matter
("Keseh" as a term for time and season)
to the matter of Rosh HaShanah,
based on the well-known teaching of the Maggid
[which is brought in the discourse of the Alter Rebbe printed in the Siddur with Chassidus11
that was written by his son and successor, the Mitteler Rebbe],
that time is created.
And from this it is understood,
that just as on Rosh HaShanah a renewal is effected in the creation of the entire world,
as the statement12
"This day is the beginning of Your works, a remembrance of the first day,"
so too, on Rosh HaShanah there is the renewal of the entire creation of the boundaries of time and place and their existence
(for time and place are boundaries of the world13).
And the matter is,
that behold, there is a known precise point
(in Likkutei Torah14
etc.),
that on the 25th of Elul the world was created15,
and on Rosh HaShanah it is the sixth day of Creation,
the day of the creation of Adam, the first man,
and what is this "This day is the beginning of Your works, a remembrance of the first day"?
And it is explained in this14,
that although the creation of the entire world was in the first moment of the six days of Creation,
as it is written16
"In the beginning, G-d created the heavens and the earth,"
and all the more so that then the boundaries of time and place and their existence were created
(for they are boundaries of the world as above),
nevertheless,
the perfection of creation was specifically on the sixth day of Creation,
the day of the creation of Adam.
Therefore specifically this day is called "the beginning of Your works and a remembrance of the first day."
And with this one will also understand that this day is called by the name "Keseh" simply,
which is a time and season,
for although the coming into being of the boundaries of time and place and their existence was in the first moment,
nevertheless, specifically on this day is the perfection of the coming into being of the boundary and existence of time
(and place),
because this is the day of the creation of Adam, the first man.
For Adam, the first man, effected perfection in all of creation through drawing down G-dliness
(His kingship)
into creation17,
for this is what is called "Adam" from the term "I will be like the Most High"18,
that he drew down His G-dliness below to make for Him a dwelling place in the lower realms within the boundaries of time and place.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Just as Adam perfected creation, so too every Jew each year draws down G-dliness, and Adam was created alone to teach that each Jewish soul is a whole world.

translations.translation: And behold, just as it was the first time,
that Adam, the first man, then effected perfection in all of creation,
including in the matter of time,
so too it is every single year through the service of each and every Jew,
who is also called "Adam" from the term "I will be like the Most High"19,
meaning that each and every Jew through his service draws down His G-dliness below.
And on the contrary,
therefore man was created alone, to teach you that whoever sustains a single soul of Israel, it is as if he sustained an entire world20,
meaning that this that Adam, the first man, was created alone,
"I will be like the Unique One of the world"
(the aspect of Yechidah, which is above the aspect of Echad21),
because of a single soul of Israel.
